# Start Here
Bijou is a TypeScript toolkit for terminal interfaces, from printable components
to fullscreen applications with layout, input, themes, and localization.

DOGFOOD is the canonical terminal documentation surface for the repository. Built in Bijou itself, the docs shell, interaction model, and examples all exercise the same medium the framework provides to users.
## What is Bijou?
Bijou combines explicit surfaces, mode-aware components, a fullscreen app
runtime, and host adapters. Applications retain their text and semantic data
when lowering visual output for different terminal capabilities.
## Documentation Map
- **Guides**: Orientation and navigation within the Bijou ecosystem.
- **Components**: The live, interactive field guide to component families and variants.
- **Packages**: Deep dives into the roles and responsibilities of each workspace package.
- **Philosophy**: Architectural doctrine, invariants, and the project's engineering stance.
- **Release**: Current-line release notes and migration guidance.
## Current Posture
The rendering foundation uses byte-packed surfaces. Allocation and performance
depend on the rendering path and application workload.
DOGFOOD combines generated component documentation, live package READMEs,
maintained guides, and historical articles from the preserved documentation
archive. Historical articles are labeled in the reader; their claims retain
their original scope. The reader is not an automatic mirror of every code change.
Open **Latest Features** for raster fonts, Markdown typography, animated theme
colors, book-matched themes, and presentation fallbacks. Open **Current Release
Story** for the running package version and release-evidence boundary. A preview
feature in this checkout does not establish stable publication.

`RasterFont` stores validated, immutable glyph coverage and advance metrics.
`layoutRasterText()` exposes positioned glyphs for effects such as DOGFOOD’s
cylinder. `rasterizeText()` returns a black-on-transparent RGBA frame, while
`rasterTextSurface()` sends that coverage through the existing Braille, quadrant
// A tiny bitmap fixture; production atlases use coverage compiled from a font.
advance: 3, left: 0, top: 0, width: 2, height: 2, columns: 2, rows: 2,
family: 'Demo', lineHeight: 3, glyphs: new Map([['A', glyph]]),
Coverage bits run row by row, least-significant bit first. Metrics share one
coordinate system: `left` and `top` are bearings relative to the glyph origin;
`advance` moves the next origin. Negative bearings and multiline text are
preserved. A font owns a copy of its lookup and each glyph owns its mask.
Unknown code points throw unless the font explicitly names a fallback glyph.
This first API performs code-point layout, without shaping, bidi or kerning.
Empty text produces a transparent 1 × 1 RGBA frame, so it can pass directly
through `rasterToGlyphSurface()`. Surface colors come from `fg` and `bg`;
coverage is monochrome and does not use the image renderer’s color sampling.
When reducing glyph coverage, the text rasterizer preserves every covered atlas
texel by marking the output pixels it overlaps. Thin stems and bars therefore
survive between output-pixel centers. At small sizes this can round a stroke
up to one pixel or close a gap smaller than one pixel. Enlargement retains
nearest-neighbor coverage. The work budget includes atlas visits and projected
pixel writes as well as output sampling.
Braille and quadrant text surfaces default to retaining any nonzero coverage
when fitting into the terminal grid. An explicit renderer `threshold` overrides
that default. Custom character sets retain the image renderer's density mapping.
Supply precompiled coverage; the renderer does not load TTF files, install fonts
or make network requests. DOGFOOD’s Jacquard 12 generator demonstrates offline
OpenType extraction and preserves the font’s license under `assets/fonts/`.
Keep a readable textual alternative for essential information in pipe and
accessible presentations: raster lettering is an illustration.
Rendering rejects more than 20,000 input code units, 1,048,576 allocated pixels,
or 16,777,216 glyph samples. Surface output is limited to 131,072 cells, 4,096
columns and 1,024 rows. Output pixel height must be an integer from 1 to 4,096.
The caller chooses its own caching policy; the library has no global font cache.

packages/bijou/README.md: # @flyingrobots/bijou
The pure, zero-dependency core of Bijou.

`@flyingrobots/bijou` provides the foundational primitives for CLIs, prompts, and portable terminal output. It manages components, themes, environment detection, and the core `Surface` and `LayoutNode` types.
## Role
- **Degradation-First**: Automatic mode detection for `interactive`, `static`, `pipe`, and `accessible` output.
- **Mixed-Mode**: High-performance `Surface` primitives for rich TUI apps, with
string-first helpers for standalone CLI scripts.
- **Surface primitives without abandoning strings**: Runtime apps can stay on
the surface path while CLI-first flows still use the string-first helpers.
- **Hexagonal Core**: Pure TypeScript logic isolated from platform IO via `Runtime`, `IO`, and `Style` ports.
## Install
```bash
npm install @flyingrobots/bijou @flyingrobots/bijou-node
## Quick Start
```typescript
import { initDefaultContext } from '@flyingrobots/bijou-node';
import { badge, boxSurface, tableSurface } from '@flyingrobots/bijou';
const ctx = initDefaultContext();
const panel = boxSurface(
tableSurface({
columns: [{ header: 'Service' }, { header: 'Status' }],
rows: [['api', badge('LIVE', { variant: 'success', ctx })]],
ctx,
title: 'Runtime',
padding: { top: 1, bottom: 1, left: 1, right: 1 },
ctx,
## Strategy: Choosing Component Families
Select the family based on the interaction semantic, not just the visual shape.
Render-path naming follows one house rule: the base family name is the public
component, and a `*Surface()` companion means “the same family on the composable
surface path.” If there is no `*Surface()` companion, the family is either
already surface-native, intentionally string-first, or both paths would be
fake duplication rather than a real second API.
### Status and Feedback
- **`badge()`**: Compact, inline status.
- **`note()`**: Non-urgent explanation.
- **`alert()`**: Persistent, in-flow message.
- **`guidedFlow()`**: Calm multi-step assistance with one explicit next action.
- **`explainability()`**: AI- or machine-mediated recommendation with visible provenance and evidence.
- *Use `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` notifications for stacking, history, or active routing.*
### Selection and Prompts
- **`select()`**: Single choice from a stable set.
- **`filter()`**: Search-led choice from a large or dynamic set.
- **`multiselect()`**: Choosing multiple values to build a set.
- **`confirm()`**: Strictly binary decisions.
### Hierarchy and Chronology
- **`tree()`**: Parent/child nesting. Indents from the right and mirrors connectors under `direction: 'rtl'`.
- **`timeline()`**: Sequential, time-ordered events.
- **`dag()`**: Causal or dependency-based graphs.
### Progress and Wayfinding
- **`progressBar()`**: Determinate completion. Takes `direction`; under `'rtl'` the fill grows from the right edge (see Layout Direction).
- **`spinner()`**: Indeterminate activity.
- **`breadcrumb()`**: Path context. Mirrors flow and separator under `direction: 'rtl'`.
- **`stepper()`**: Ordered stages in a linear process. Steps run right to left under `direction: 'rtl'`.
### Theme Authoring
- **`extendTheme(base, extensions)`**: Build a custom theme from a known-good
preset. All six groups are optional overrides: `status`, `ui`, `gradient`,
`surface`, `border`, and `semantic`. The latter two accept
`Partial<Theme['border']>` and `Partial<Theme['semantic']>` and preserve
omitted preset tokens. Their keys are fixed; `status`, `ui`, and `gradient`
also support additional keys.
- **`defineThemeSafePairs()`**: Declare reusable foreground/background
contrast matrices for `doctorTheme()` and inspector surfaces.
- **`doctorTheme()`**: Structured checks for invalid colors, weak contrast,
and suspicious token reuse.
- **`themeContrastRatio()`**: Deterministic foreground/background contrast
calculation for token-pair tests.
- **`createSapphireReferencePalette()`**: Inspect or explore the shared
hue-anchored references behind `BIJOU_DARK` and `BIJOU_LIGHT`.
- **Perceptual color helpers**: Convert sRGB, OKLAB, and OKLCH with
`rgbToOklab()`, `rgbToOklch()`, `oklabToRgb()`, and `oklchToRgb()`; use
`gamutMapOklch()` or `gamutRelativeOklch()` to stay inside sRGB; compare
colors with `deltaEOk()`; and interpolate circular hue with
`interpolateHue()`.
### Sapphire Noir First-Party Defaults
The legacy `CYAN_MAGENTA` preset is useful as a vivid terminal-native preset,
but it is not ideal as the model for dense product surfaces. It uses saturated
terminal colors for many unrelated jobs: cyan appears as info, active state,
cursor, scrollbar, logo, and primary border; magenta appears as accent,
secondary border, and focus gutter. That makes the app energetic, but it also
makes many regions compete at the same visual priority.
Bijou's `BIJOU_DARK` and `BIJOU_LIGHT` defaults are one derived **Sapphire
Noir** system. They use a calmer shell posture:
- neutral surfaces carry most of the screen
- one accent family carries local emphasis and shell selection
- status colors remain distinct from focus and brand
- muted text remains contrast-safe instead of merely dim
- dark and light themes both satisfy readable foreground/background pairs
The dark preset leads with low-chroma graphite surfaces, ice-neutral text, and
a luminous sapphire focus color. The light preset keeps the intentional warm
surface family as porcelain while using darker sapphire for interactive
chrome. Amber is reserved for warning; green, red, and cool violet retain
success, error, and information. Focus therefore no longer masquerades as a
warning, and informational status no longer collapses into brand chrome.
The optional `DOGFOOD` shell theme family exposes these library defaults in
`Dark` and `Light` modes. The docs app opens with its separate Bijou Book theme
family; selecting DOGFOOD demonstrates the first-party Sapphire palette.
Both Sapphire modes target at least 4.5:1 contrast for surface text and common
semantic foregrounds on every shell surface.
#### Perceptual derivation
The first-party references are generated from `SAPPHIRE_HUE` (`255` degrees)
and mode-specific lightness/chroma curves. Chroma is expressed as a fraction
of the sRGB gamut boundary at the chosen OKLCH lightness and hue. This keeps a
relative chroma of `1` in gamut and avoids the hue shifts caused by clipping
RGB channels after conversion.
```ts
import { createSapphireReferencePalette } from '@flyingrobots/bijou';
const references = createSapphireReferencePalette('dark');
const customReferences = createSapphireReferencePalette('light', {
brandHue: 265,
The public color-math floor uses normalized OKLAB lightness (`0..1`), OKLCH
chroma (`0` or greater), and hue in degrees. `gamutRelativeOklch()` clamps its
relative-chroma argument to `0..1`; `gamutMapOklch()` preserves normalized
lightness and hue while reducing out-of-gamut chroma. `interpolateHue()` takes
a progress value clamped to `0..1` and an explicit `shorter` or `longer` arc;
when longer-path endpoints normalize to the same hue, it travels one complete
turn. Use `deltaEOk()` for fast ordinary design-distance checks, not
high-precision colorimetry. Numeric helpers reject malformed tuples and
non-finite channels rather than emitting an invalid color.
The conversion matrices follow Björn Ottosson's
[OKLAB reference](https://bottosson.github.io/posts/oklab/). The
boundary-relative chroma model applies the same practical shell concept
documented by [nutelch](https://github.com/meodai/nutelch), implemented here by
a small deterministic binary search so Bijou keeps its zero-dependency core.
Rule-authored themes retain inspectable authoring definitions.
`renameRuleAuthoredTheme(theme, name)` creates a renamed theme while preserving
that provenance; `ruleAuthoredDefinitions(theme)` returns its immutable
snapshot, or `undefined` for themes without registered authoring data.
`tokenDefinitionPaths(definitions)` lists authored token paths.
`collectTokenDependents(definitions, mode)` reports direct consumers;
`collectTransitiveTokenDependents(definitions, mode)` follows the full chain.
These maps select the requested adaptive branch, omit unresolved references
and inspect dependencies without evaluating cyclic token values.
They include inspection inputs such as excluded candidates whose colors remain
visible in provenance; an edge does not promise that every edit changes the
selected hex value.
DOGFOOD's Theme Lab uses this provenance to show rules, candidates, scores,
contrast and direct draft overrides alongside a live component specimen.
It stacks its panels below the two-column width floor. A direct override is
reported separately from a value that changed through propagation; this view
does not claim every edit triggers complete graph-driven recomputation.
### Mode-Aware Authoring
`NO_COLOR` disables color without changing detected interactivity. Unknown
status keys fall back to `semantic.muted`.
- **`renderByMode()`**: Dispatch a component to the current output contract.
- **`lintModeLowering()`**: Compare explicit semantic facts across output modes.
- **`modeLoweringReportText()`**: Render a compact lowering report for tests,
docs, and review comments.
- **`defineComponentMetadata()`**: Declare validated package, family, mode,
arg, variant, invariant, example, and source facts for tooling.
- **`componentMetadataSummary()`**: Render compact metadata for docs, MCP
payloads, and agent-facing reports.
- **`defineBlock()`**: Declare a validated reusable block with package, family,
scale, mode, slot, variant, config, component, story, semantic facts, optional
view data contracts, and command intents.
- **`standardBlocks` / standard block exports**: Import the first-party
standard block definitions for AppShell, ReaderSurface, InspectorPanel,
inline status, in-flow status, transient overlay feedback, activity stream,
shortcut cues, and progress. These expose contracts, stories, data
requirements, command intents, and schema-bound posture, with deterministic
first-proof render output across all output modes. Production AppShell
behavior remains a later runtime slice.
- **`defineBlockPackage()`**: Declare exported blocks, docs, tags, version, and
Bijou peer compatibility for ordinary NPM block packages.
- **`defineBlockSchemaAdapter()` / `defineSchemaBlock()`**: Validate unknown
boundary data before producing immutable block render input and binding facts,
without fetching, subscribing, dispatching, or rendering AppShell.
- **`blockMetadataSummary()`**: Render compact block metadata for docs, MCP
payloads, and agent-facing reports.
- **`defineAppShellComposition()`**: Compose runtime-backed blocks into logical
AppShell slots with an explicit provider scope, without rendering or
subscribing.
- **`blockRenderNode()` / `renderBlockTree()`**: Explicitly render nested block
declarations into parent slots when a preview or host intentionally wants a
block tree, while ordinary `block.render()` remains a local single-block
render contract.
- **`defineDataRequirement()` / `defineDataProvider()` / `providerScope()`**:
Declare data requirements and explicit local provider availability without
hidden global registration.
- **`defineViewData()`**: Group named data requirements for a view or block
without binding them to providers.
- **`resolveProviderRequirement()`**: Resolve a requirement against an explicit
local provider scope as frozen metadata, without subscribing or fetching.
- **`bindingFrameFromSnapshots()`**: Assemble read-only render frames from
resolved provider metadata and already-created immutable snapshots.
- **`bindingSnapshot()` / `bindingFrame()`**: Model provider-delivered plain
data as copied, versioned immutable snapshots and read-only render frames.
- **`commandIntent()`**: Declare user intent outputs as inspectable metadata,
without business-logic callbacks or provider mutation handles.
- **`captureStoryMatrix()`**: Capture every profile/variant pair from a story
renderer.
- **`storyCaptureMatrixText()`**: Render a deterministic multi-mode story
matrix for docs and tests.
- **`createFixturePromotionRecord()`**: Preserve provenance when a fixture,
docs page, story, example, or MCP payload is promoted into another surface.
- **`fixturePromotionText()`**: Render that promotion record for review and
agent output.
### Layout Direction
Direction-sensitive Components read one resolved inline direction (R26:
think in start and end, not left and right).
- **`direction` option / `ctx.direction`**: Component options that extend
`BijouNodeOptions` accept `direction?: 'ltr' | 'rtl'`; `createBijou()` and
`createTestContext()` accept a context-wide `direction`.
- **`resolveDirection(options)`**: The single resolver. The explicit option
overrides the context; absent both, the direction is `'ltr'`.
- **`mirrorsLayout(options)`**: True only for `'rtl'` in `interactive` and
`static` modes. `pipe` and `accessible` output keep logical order.
- **`directionalSide('start' | 'end', direction)`** and
**`orderForDirection(items, direction)`**: Map logical edges to physical
sides and logical sequences to visual order without mutating the input.
- **`mirrorGlyph(glyph, direction)`** and **`mirrorGlyphs(text, direction)`**:
Swap directional glyphs (‹ ›, « », ▸ ◂, ▶ ◀, → ←, ⇒ ⇐ and similar) under
`'rtl'`. Pass only Component-owned affordances; never code, paths, IDs,
commands or URLs. ASCII `<` and `>` are never swapped.
- **Mirrored Components**: `tree()`, `enumeratedList()` and `accordion()` indent from the right under `'rtl'`, padded to their widest line.
Mirrored Components:
- **`progressBar()`**: Under `'rtl'` in `interactive` and `static` output the
fill grows from the right edge, the gradient's leading edge is the rightmost
cell, and the percentage label moves to the right, flush against the bar
(`⠐⠐⠐⠐⠐█████ 50% `). The label text is never reversed. The fill is whole
cells only (`round(percent / 100 * width)`), so there is no partial-block
glyph to mirror and precision is `1 / width` in both directions. Caller
`filled` and `empty` glyphs pass through `mirrorGlyphs()` (`▶` becomes `◀`);
symmetric glyphs, including ASCII `#`, `-`, `>` and `<`, are unchanged, so an
ASCII fallback needs no mapping. `pipe` (`Progress: 45%`) and `accessible`
(`45 percent complete.`) output are identical in both directions.
Components that read the direction today:
- **`box()`, `headerBox()`, `boxSurface()`, `headerBoxSurface()`**: Under a
resolved `'rtl'` direction in `interactive` and `static` modes the title in
the top border sits at the right edge (the logical start) instead of the
left. A title too long for the border is clipped exactly as in `'ltr'`, then
aligned the same way. Title text is never reversed, and `pipe` and
`accessible` output keep their plain logical form. These components have no
title-alignment option; a title is always at the logical start edge.
Illustrative composition for a direction-sensitive Component; per-family
integration is tracked separately:
```ts
const visual = mirrorsLayout(options) ? 'rtl' : 'ltr';
const separator = mirrorGlyphs(' › ', visual);
const items = orderForDirection(crumbs, visual);
### Profunctor Page Inspection
- **`lowerProfunctorPageArtifacts()`**: Validate one canonical
`profunctor-page/0`, `profunctor-page-source-map/0`, and
`profunctor-build-manifest/0` family, then emit a deterministic
`ui-scene-ir/1` scene, terminal `Surface`, target map, receipt, and text
witness.
- **`ProfunctorPageTargetError`**: Inspect stable `code`, `path`, and `detail`
fields when the bounded ProjectPage target rejects malformed,
contradictory, or unsupported input.
- **[Profunctor Page Inspection reference](../../docs/book/bijou-designs.pdf#page=425)**:
Review the exact input versions, supported blocks, inspection modes, output

### Browser Renderer Seam
- **`lowerUiSceneToBrowser()`**: Lower a `ui-scene-ir/1` scene with a
`geordi-browser` target profile to a deterministic element tree and HTML
markup. The output holds only facts the scene declares.
- **`createUiSceneBrowserDom()`**: Build that tree through a host document.
- **`createUiSceneBrowserReceipt()`**: Record the browser output in a
`ui-scene-receipt/1`.
- **[Browser renderer seam reference](../../docs/topics/ui-scene-browser/README.md)**:
Review the element mapping, options, refusals, and limits.
### Terminal and Browser Parity Witness
- **`witnessUiSceneParity()`**: Lower one `ui-scene-ir/1` scene on the
terminal target and on the browser target, then report each fact as equal, a
named gap, or a mismatch.
- **`compareUiSceneLowerings()`**: Compare a terminal lowering and a browser
lowering that already exist.
- **[Parity witness reference](../../docs/topics/ui-scene-parity/README.md)**:
Review the facts that must be equal, the named gaps, and the limits.

packages/create-bijou-tui-app/README.md: Scaffold a new Bijou TUI app with batteries-included defaults.
- **Canonical starter** — generated apps target the current `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui` + `@flyingrobots/bijou-tui-app` path instead of an older shell-starter path.
- **Public API only** — the scaffolded app uses public package APIs so it can serve as a downstream canary for real-world upgrades.
- **Release-aligned defaults** — the generated project matches the same shell/runtime split described in the root docs and migration guide.
The generated app can also be run directly with:
- A README that explains the shell patterns the starter is modeling
- `-y`, `--yes`, `--force`: allow writing into a non-empty target directory
## Test this scaffolder locally (from this monorepo)
# Validate the stock generated scaffold end-to-end from packed local tarballs
# Smoke-test generated files without installing dependencies

The canary smoke run is the strongest downstream check: it generates the stock scaffold, rewrites only the Bijou dependency specs to local tarballs, builds the app, and drives the shipped shell through tab switches, drawer toggles, resizes, and quit-confirm flows under a PTY.
The generated app is intentionally opinionated:
- the drawer models supplemental side work
- the split page models comparison and inspection
Use this scaffolder when you want a real shell starter, not just an empty `run(app)` bootstrap.

For upgrade notes and architecture context, see [`../../docs/MIGRATING_TO_V4.md`](../../docs/book/bijou-designs.pdf#page=322) and [`../../docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`](../../docs/book/bijou-designs.pdf#page=141).
See the [Bijou repo](https://github.com/flyingrobots/bijou) for the full documentation map, architecture guide, and design system.
